first.title: Sign in with Kerberos
first.heading: Sign in with a Kerberos ticket
first.lead: This service asked your client for a Kerberos ticket (WWW-Authenticate: Negotiate, RFC 4559). If it has one, or can get one, it will repeat this request with it and you will be signed in without typing anything.
waiting.title: Kerberos: one more round trip
waiting.heading: 401 — the negotiation is not finished
waiting.note: Your client should answer this reply with another token. If you are reading this page, it did not — the exchange is unfinished rather than refused.
ifNothing.heading: If nothing happened
ifNothing.browsers: Most browsers send Negotiate only to hosts on an explicit allow-list, and the machine needs a Kerberos credential cache in this realm besides. In Chrome that is --auth-server-allowlist; in Firefox it is network.negotiate-auth.trusted-uris. Without both, what you see is this page and no ticket is ever requested — which is not a failure of anything here, and is why the link above exists.
ifNothing.program: A program does not have this problem: get a ticket for the service principal named below and send it as Authorization: Negotiate <base64>. That is all this endpoint is.
fallback.none: Nothing sent you here, so there is nothing to go back to. This door can be used on its own — a client that holds a ticket gets a session and no application had to ask.
fallback.stillWaiting: — the request that sent you here is still waiting, and it will carry on either way.
signedIn.title: Signed in
signedIn.heading: 200 — you are signed in
signedIn.as: Signed in as {name}, from the Kerberos principal {principal}.
signedIn.cookie: The session cookie is set. Every protocol this service speaks reads the same session, so an /oauth2/authorize, a wsignin1.0, a SAML AuthnRequest or the admin console will now complete without asking you for anything.
signedIn.subject: Subject
signedIn.noAmr: — the ticket claims no pre-authentication, so this service claims no authentication method
signedIn.bare: — a bare Kerberos token, no negotiation
signedIn.usersRow: now has a row for this person, and the embedded directory has an entry.
refusal.wrong-scheme: Your browser answered with an Authorization header for another scheme, not Negotiate, so no Kerberos ticket was presented.
refusal.empty-token: Your browser sent Negotiate with no token after it, so there was no ticket to check.
refusal.undecodable: What your browser sent after Negotiate is neither a SPNEGO token nor a Kerberos one, so it could not be read.
refusal.no-common-mechanism: Your browser offered only mechanisms this service does not perform, so the negotiation could not agree on Kerberos.
refusal.non-kerberos-mechanism: The mechanism your browser chose is not one this service performs; only Kerberos is.
refusal.acceptor-threw: This service failed while checking your Kerberos ticket, so you were not signed in.
refusal.ticket-refused: Your Kerberos ticket did not pass one of the checks this service makes, so you were not signed in. The table below says which.
refusal.bad-mech-list-mic: The negotiation's integrity check (the mechListMIC, RFC 4178 section 5) did not verify, so the exchange was refused.
refusal.mic-required: The negotiation required an integrity check (a mechListMIC, RFC 4178 section 5) and your browser sent none.
refusal.no-pending-continuation: Your browser continued a negotiation this service has no record of, so there was nothing to continue.
refusal.continuation-no-mic: Your browser's continuation of the negotiation carried no mechListMIC, which it must.
refusal.general: Your Kerberos ticket did not sign you in.
refusal.policy: Your Kerberos ticket verified, but this service will not start a session for this identity.
refusal.failed: Something went wrong on this service during the Kerberos sign-in, so you were not signed in.
background.refused: This address signs a person in with a Kerberos ticket their browser presents (SPNEGO, RFC 4559). The ticket was presented and refused, so no session was started. Presenting the same ticket again will be refused the same way; signing in with a username works whatever the ticket did.
background.policy: That is a policy decision rather than anything wrong with the ticket, the KDC or the service principal, and presenting the ticket again will not change it. Whoever administers this service decides which roles an application requires.
background.failed: The failure is this service's, not your ticket's. Trying again may work; if it does not, send the diagnostics below to whoever runs this service.
